''26. He commaunded.''] The Churche (here signified by the boate or shippe) and Catholikes, are often tossed with stormes of persecution, but Christ who seemed to sleepe in the meane time, by the Churches prayers awaketh, and maketh a calme.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. IX.}}}}}}

{{c|''The Maisters of the Iewes he confuteth both with reasons and miracles: 2. defending his remitting of sinnes, 9. his eating with sinners, 14. and his condescending to his weake Disciples vntil he haue made them stronger. 18. shewing also in two miracles, the order of his prouidence about the Iewes and Gentils, leauing the one when he called the other. 27. he cureth tvvo blind men, and one possessed. 35. And hauing with so many miracles together confuted his enemies, and yet they worse and worse, vpon pitie toward the people, he thinketh of sending true pastours vnto them.''}} {{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=9|verse=1}}}}ND {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpon the 18 Sunday after Pentecost.}}entring into a boate, he passed ouer the vvater, and came into his ovvne citie. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=2}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 2, 3. Luc. 5, 18.''}}* behold they brought to him one sicke of the palsey lying in bedde. And {{sc|Iesvs}} {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ We see that the fayth of one helpeth to obtaine for an other.}}∷ seeing their faith, said to the sicke of the palsey, Haue a good hart sonne, thy sinnes are forgiuen thee. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=3}}† And behold certaine of the Scribes sayd vvithin them selues, {{sup|‖}} He blasphemeth. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=4}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} seeing their thoughtes, said. Wherfore thinke you euil in your hartes? {{verse|chapter=9|verse=5}}† {{sup|‖}} Whether is easier, to say, thy sinnes are forgiuen thee: or to say, Arise and vvalke? {{verse|chapter=9|verse=6}}† But that you may know that {{sup|‖}} the Sonne of man hath povver in earth to forgiue sinnes, (then sayd he to the sicke of the palsey,) Arise, take vp thy bedde, and goe into thy house. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=7}}† And he arose, and vvent into his house. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=8}}† And the multitudes seeing it, vvere afrayd, and {{sup|‖}} glorified God that gaue such povver {{sup|‖}} to men.⊣

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=9}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō S. Matthewes day.}}And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mar. 2, 14. Luc. 5, 27.''}}* vvhen {{sc|Iesvs}} passed forth from thence, he savv a man sitting in the custome-house, named Matthevv: And he sayth to him, Folovv me. And he arose vp, and folovved him. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=10}}† And it came to passe as he vvas sitting at meate in the house, behold many Publicans and sinners came, and sate dovvne vvith {{sc|Iesvs}} and his Disciples. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=11}}† And the Pharisees seeing it, sayd to his Disciples: vvhy doth your Master eate vvith Publicans & sinners? {{verse|chapter=9|verse=12}}† But {{sc|Iesvs}} hearing it, sayd: They that are in health, neede not a physicion, but they that are il at ease. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=13}}† But go your vvayes and learne vvhat it is, ''I vvil mercie, & {{sup|‖}} not sacrifice''. For I am not come to cal the iust, but sinners.⊣ {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Ose. 6, 6.''}}

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=14}}† Then {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mar. 2, 18. Lu. 5, 33.''}}* came to him the Disciples of Iohn, saying, vvhy do vve and the Pharisees {{sup|‖}} fast often, but thy Disciples do not<noinclude>{{rh|||fast?}}</noinclude>
